definition: The tendency of a neural network to lose previously learned information when it is trained on new data or tasks.
details: Catastrophic forgetting is a challenge in continual and fine-tuning scenarios, motivating techniques like rehearsal, regularization-based methods, or parameter-efficient fine-tuning that preserve prior knowledge.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Catastrophic Forgetting.
